concepts.def: Daily routine uses reflexive verbs: me despierto (I wake up), me levanto (I get up), me ducho (I shower), me acuesto (I go to bed).
Meals vocabulary: el desayuno, la comida or el almuerzo (lunch), la cena, with verbs desayunar, almorzar and cenar.
Telling the time: 'Es la una', 'Son las dos y media', and saying when things happen with 'a las ocho'.
School-day vocabulary: las clases, los deberes (homework), el recreo (break), and 'Las clases empiezan a las nueve'.
Household chores: hacer la cama (make the bed), poner la mesa (set the table), sacar la basura (take out the rubbish).
Stem-changing verbs alter their vowel: empezar gives empiezo, and acostarse gives me acuesto (o changes to ue).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area A: Everyday Activities — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area A: Everyday Activities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area A: Everyday Activities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does 'me levanto a las siete' mean?
options: I get up at seven
I go to bed at seven
I eat lunch at seven
I leave school at seven

mcqs.q: 'Son las siete y cuarto' tells you the time is what?
Which is the correct first-person form of 'acostarse'?
options: Me acuesto
Me acosto
Acuesto me
Me acostar
To set the table
To clear the snow
To do the shopping
To make the bed

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I get up' in Spanish?
options: Just 'levanto', dropping the reflexive pronoun.
Almorzaron.
Me levanto - the reflexive pronoun is needed because you raise yourself.
Voy levantar.

mcqs.q: How do you say it is one o'clock?
options: Voy levantar.
'Hay la una.'
'Es la una' - one o'clock takes the singular verb and article.
'Son las una', using the plural as for all other hours.

mcqs.q: What is the correct yo-form of 'almorzar' (to have lunch)?
options: Almorzo, keeping the spelling of the infinitive.
'Hay la una.'
Almuerzo - the o changes to ue in the stem.
Almorzaron.
